items.q: Why rename to-PRD → to-spec and to-issues → to-tickets?
items.a: What it produced was never a true PRD — a **spec** is the broader destination doc. **Tickets** (not GitHub/Linear "issues") are the journey to enact it. Precise naming is **"good friction"** that shapes what leaks into each document. Re-run `npx skills add mattpocock/skills` and prune stale skills.

items.q: What full lifecycle does v1.1 complete?
items.a: **Grill → spec → tickets → `/implement` → code review.** Implement stays deliberately tiny: **TDD at pre-agreed seams**, typecheck regularly, full suite once at end, then review + commit. Repo: ~**160K stars**, ~**7M downloads**.

items.q: When should you use Wayfinder instead of one giant grill session?
items.a: When a loose idea is **"too big for one agent session and wrapped in fog."** It charts a GitHub issue map with **blocking sub-issues**, each scoped to one session — close a session, open the next ticket; feed the completed map to **to-spec**.

items.q: What ticket types does Wayfinder use?
items.a: **Research** (AFK background agent), **grilling** (human-in-the-loop), **prototype** (cheap concrete artifact), and **task** (boring human config that can't be automated). Matt uses it "for literally everything."

items.q: Why are ~10 lines of Martin Fowler smells "outrageously useful"?
items.a: *Refactoring* vocabulary is **deep in agent priors** — mysterious name, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, message chains, middle man. One sentence per smell makes the reviewer **name and fix** them.

In a repo **`coding-standards.md`**, **outside AGENTS.md**, pushed to the reviewer. Review runs **two parallel sub-agents**: standards conformance + **spec fidelity**. Refactoring is **review's job**, not TDD's (red-green only, one slice at a time).

items.q: What grilling bugs did v1.1 fix?
items.a: Explain **why one question at a time**; add a **confirmation gate** before implementation; distinguish **facts** (explore the codebase yourself) from **decisions** (user must choose) — especially stops **Fable** from grilling itself.

items.q: When should you prototype before writing a spec?
items.a: Especially for **front-end**: raise discussion fidelity with a **cheap, rough, concrete artifact** to react to — via `/prototype` and `/research` against primary sources.
